topic: termites eat more than old wood
myth: Termites only attack old wooden houses.
actually: They eat anything with cellulose: doors, cupboards, books, even cardboard boxes.
caption:
Think termites are only an old-house problem? 🪵

Termites feed on cellulose, so modern flats with wooden doors, modular cupboards, books and stored cardboard boxes are on the menu too.

Tap your door frames and skirting now and then. A hollow sound is worth a closer look.

takeaway: That's why one spray is never the end. Treat the source, not just the sighting.
caption:
One cockroach egg case can hold 30–40 eggs.

So when you spray the one you see, the next generation is already waiting in a crack behind the fridge. Lasting control means treating where they breed.

fact_text: Dengue mosquitoes breed in clean, still water
action_text: Empty, scrub & dry every water holder weekly
caption:
The 7-day rule that keeps dengue mosquitoes away 🦟

Aedes mosquitoes breed in small pools of clean, still water and can go from egg to biting adult in about a week. Empty, scrub and dry flower-pot trays, cooler tanks, AC drip trays and terrace buckets every 7 days.

headline: Where cockroaches hide
caption:
Cockroaches love three things: warmth, water and darkness. Your kitchen has all three.

Check behind the fridge, under the sink and around drains. Droppings like ground pepper or a musty smell mean they've moved in.

It can spread dengue, bites mostly in the daytime, and breeds in clean water around your home. The easiest win? Don't give it water to breed in.

headline: Your question this week.

messages.text: Do we have to leave home during pest control?
Gel baits for cockroaches & ants: stay home, carry on as usual.
Sprays: keep kids & pets out of treated rooms until surfaces dry.

fact_text: Gel = stay. Spray = wait till dry
action_text: DM a question. We answer every Sunday
caption:
Ask HyZone: "Do we have to leave home during pest control?"

It depends on the treatment. Gel baits: carry on as usual. Sprays: keep kids and pets out of treated rooms until surfaces are dry. Your technician will tell you exactly how long.
